node_definition.done_when: Read section 26 of crew-observability-truth first, and its two comments: b88a904a9 already landed the exited-unfinished state, crew repair-status, and the worker stop hook accepting a waiting manifest. The remaining defect: a manifest declaring a well-formed wait (a job-id wait with an squeue probe, as on run r-20261002T053506691175-fsri-frozen-newton-terminal-residual) is classified unreadable when an unrelated audit check fails, for example the gate log first-line check. That blocks the automatic resume. The classification in reckon/crew/runs.py, fed by audit_manifest in reckon/crew/reports.py, reads such a run as waiting. The audit finding is reported beside that state as an attached finding, never in place of it. A manifest whose wait block itself is malformed still reads unreadable. tests/test_valid_wait_keeps_its_state.py, in a temporary RECKON_HOME, builds a manifest with a valid job-id wait plus a failing gate-log first-line check. It asserts the run classifies waiting and carries the audit finding. It also asserts that a malformed wait block still classifies unreadable. The first case fails at the base revision. Existing tests that reach audit_manifest or the run classification keep passing; grep tests/ for audit_manifest and for the classification function to build the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/valid-wait-keeps-its-state.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
